questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- The curriculum and reputation of the Economics department at this university: whether courses offered match with my interest of study
- Position (a place not too close to my home university so that I could experience new cultures) and living expenses (should not be a metropolitan area, so that I could afford to live there)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The communication was very clear and direct. We had an orientation and had the chance to ask the head of department everything we need about the program. In addition, we had a faculty member who took responsibilities about our problems, who we can go directly to the office and asked for her help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
-Orientation day
-Supervisor
-Lots of information in their website

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: However, I still have no idea why I got rejected by CROUS to stay in one of their dorms while 99% of exchange students in my course got it. Finding an apartment to live in just a short time is not an easy task and though I managed to do so, it still does not make sense to me why I needed to go through that.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not quite easy. Firstly, I was waiting for CROUS, but then, close to the date of departure, they rejected me. Therefore, I needed to find the apartment through my own network (there is a moderate community of Vietnamese students in Toulouse, which I was lucky to be able to get access to). I heard stories from others, who do not want to stay in CROUS because of its hygiene conditions, and they told me that it was not that easy to find housing in only 5 months; mostly, it was overpriced or they could not find anything (they applied for all apartments on online websites, but needed to wait for like, forever)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I do not think that on campus housing is even a choice in TSE. The best thing they could get is to be accepted to CROUS. If not, then try everything they could to find a good apartment. I suggest to live near the university, which is safe and requires less effort to go to school as well as less transportation expenses. VeloToulouse is also a very good choice to go everywhere.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
For required courses, it was very easy. Students will get in no matter what.
For elective courses, it is limited to only some students based on their current transcripts. 
For some special courses, in my case, I want to take some M2 courses, it is important to get permission from head of department as well as professor of that courses. But they were all very nice to let me in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I have a supervisor who helps with all the registration so I was very smooth.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I sucessfully got in everything.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was very easy so no need to be worried about that. However, elective courses are limited so it is important to keep a suffieciently high GPA to get in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 6 courses in M1 and 4 courses in M2. I think M1 is too easy for a Master's level, while I am more interested in M2 courses because they are more focused on econometric methods.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They are quite compatible, although the classes are much smaller. In all my M2 courses, we have only 3 students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Game theory, Environmental economics, Markov chains and applications, Probability modeling,  Experimental economics, Market power and regulation, Programming in Python, Empirical industrial organization, Nonparametric Econometric Method, Econometric method for Empirical Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I like all M2 courses that I took, especially Empirical Industrial Organization, Nonparametric Econometric Method, Econometric method for Empirical Economics, because they taught lots of new econometric methods with practical projects to implement them. However, it depends on your interest, because there are also several M2 courses based on your field.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation fee, I was living near the university, so it did not take much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They have a lot of parties for exchange students, which I saw through their Instagram page. However, I am not quite interested in them.
Besides, I do not speak French, so taking part in activities I want seems impossible, like the Economics magazine or the research club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I have no idea about that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel. Toulouse is close to a lot of lovely cities, like Albi, Montpellier, or even further Barcelona etc. SNCF also have offers for 1 euro trip in first week of the month so take advanatge of them to the fullest.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have no problems with cultural differences. People here are all very nice, although I do not speak any French.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No at all.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are all very welcoming, even to a stranger. They smiled and said hi to me anytime they saw me in my apartment, and outside, people always noticed and helped me if I had any problems. I love the atmosphere here in Toulouse.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Do not hesitate to ask for permission to take an M2 course, professors here are all very nice.
- Live near the school and try to search for housing as soon as possible.
- Got a scooter or bicycle because the cycling route here is very complete.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No I dont think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned lots of things from my M2 courses. In addition, the winter weather there is much more bearable than in Copenhagen (sorry...). I also loved all the trips in Southern Europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the first month of my exchange, I have to fill in the new OLA after registration. However, it took to0 much time for my OLA to get accepted from UCPH. I need to call student service and then send an email to prove it is very urgent because it is close to mid-term, and after that, I can not change my courses anymore if I get rejected for any courses. Luckily, I did it just in time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
